canada.title: Fredericton Exhibition still hopeful for deal with city on expropriation
canada.summary: The organization across the negotiating table from the City of Fredericton says a deal is still possible over the expropriation of land on the Exhibition Grounds.

canada.title: Ukraine urges countries to follow Canada’s lead in barring Russian athletes
canada.summary: Ukraine's sports minister wants other countries to follow Canada's lead in blocking Russian teams from international hockey tournaments.

canada.title: N.B. woman fighting for coverage of opioid addiction treatment when moving provinces
canada.summary: Angela Feener, who lives in Shediac, says she feels like she has to keep paying for her apartment on Prince Edward Island and travelling back there monthly because her treatment for opioid use disorder isn't covered in New Brunswick.

canada.title: CUPE school workers vote to ratify deal with N.S.
canada.summary: Nelson Scott, president of CUPE Local 5050 in Cape Breton, confirmed the result to CBC News on Thursday night. The union's members include early childhood educators, janitors, librarians and bus drivers.

canada.title: A seasonal highway closure may be holding back tourism in Alberta’s Foothills
canada.summary: A section of Highway 40 is set to close for the winter on Dec. 1, leading some businesses in Alberta's Foothills to suggest keeping the roadway open year-round. But questions remain about the cost of winter maintenance and the potential impact on wildlife.

canada.title: Canada donates to preserve tropical forests, remains top importer of Brazil’s gold
canada.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada will give $560 million to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility.

canada.title: Stewiacke weighs cost of amalgamation studies
canada.summary: Stewiacke's mayor says there's still little known about possible amalgamation after a survey on staying independent or joining another municipality drew few responses

canada.title: Police watchdog clears RCMP officer in 2024 fatal shooting at Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation
canada.summary: The Serious Incident Response Team says it found no grounds to believe an offence was committed by the officer who shot and killed a man on Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation on Sept. 8, 2024.

canada.title: Ottawa deems Whitehorse Power Centres project of national interest
canada.summary: The federal government has named the Whitehorse Power Centres as a project of national interest. It came during the Prime Minister's visit Thursday.

canada.title: Supreme Court of Canada upholds Quebec’s secularism law
canada.summary: In a historic judgment, the Supreme Court of Canada has upheld Quebec’s Bill 21, the province’s controversial secularism law that prevents public servants from wearing religious symbols while on the job.

canada.title: Quebec to carry out audit into Churchill River deal. Wakeham vows he won’t accept changes
canada.summary: As Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says his government will carry out an internal audit of the Churchill Falls river power agreement, N.L. Premier Tony Wakeham says he’s confident the deal will carry through.

canada.title: N.W.T. health authority CEO leaves position effective immediately
canada.summary: The government of the Northwest Territories announced Thursday that Kimberly Riles is leaving her position effective immediately and that deputy minister of health and social services Alan Doody will serve as interim CEO.

canada.title: N.L. adds to Churchill River power negotiation oversight committee
canada.summary: Utility lawyer Geoffrey Young is joining the committee overseeing the final stage of negotiations for contracts for the Churchill River power deal. Opposition members say it's not what they expected for improved oversight of negotiations, or independent review of the deal.

canada.title: Some schools in Quebec close amid freezing rain warnings
canada.summary: Freezing rain Friday morning could lead to icy roads across parts of Quebec, according to Environment Canada.

canada.title: Flu season off to an early start, but microbiologist says still worth getting the shot
canada.summary: People may have been caught off guard by the early start of respiratory virus season — but one infectious disease researcher says it's not too late for Manitobans to get the flu shot.

canada.title: Sentencing hearing to continue for Kenneth Law, who admitted to aiding suicide
canada.summary: A sentencing hearing is set to continue Friday for an Ontario man who sold potentially deadly substances online to people who then used those products to take their own lives.
canada.outlet: Global News + CityNews + CBC News (CP), CP24

canada.title: Trina Hunt’s family alleges husband killed her, seeks return of assets in B.C. lawsuit
canada.summary: A new civil claim alleges Iain Hunt killed his wife and should be barred from benefiting financially from her death. The allegations have not been proven in court.
